cases.note: The user does not answer follow-up questions, so a single turn matches the scenario.

assertions.assertion: Uses the compact form of about 1,200 words with assumed answers stated, rather than the full template.
assertions.quote: It's one page and marked draft
assertions.reason: The document is a full template with many sections (constraints table, decisions table, floor/depth table, phase 2, open decisions), not a compact ~1,200-word form; the assumed answers are stated but the compactness is not shown.

assertions.assertion: States three to five one-line contracts (for example answers come from the policy, unsupported questions say so, spend stops at the cap) with where each is enforced and checked.
assertions.quote: | C1 | Every policy claim cites a page present in the policy text; ... | C5 | Text inside the PDF is data, not instructions. | Structural: no tool, so injected text cannot act. | G03/A5 |
assertions.reason: It states five contracts with enforcement and checks, but they are not all one-line (C1 and C4 are multi-sentence) and the spend contract is enforced by an external quota, so it only loosely meets the assertion.

assertions.assertion: Does not add confirmation, idempotency, rights or recovery contracts the read-only journey does not need.
assertions.quote: | Writes, personal data | n/a: read only, public PDF | Any booking or expense feature |
assertions.reason: No confirmation, idempotency, rights or recovery contracts were added; writes were marked n/a.

assertions.assertion: Has each phase 1 goal cite the contracts its acceptance proves.
assertions.quote: **G02. Agent running in `adk web`.** ... Contracts: C2, C4, D2. ... Acceptance: A1 the lisbon question gets an answer; A2 the agent has no tools and the path is not user-controlled; A3 project quota is set
assertions.reason: Each phase 1 goal lists the contracts it covers, and the acceptance checks tie back to them (G03 cites C1, C3, C5; G04 is the exception with no contracts).

assertions.assertion: Every phase 1 goal and every ticket file carries a human-effort estimate as a range, stated as hours for a developer working with a coding agent, split into hands-on and review-and-verify time.
assertions.quote: G04 OCR for scanned pages: `adk-memory-architecture`, 1–3 h; acceptance: coverage report shows zero unreviewed scanned pages.
assertions.reason: Phase 1 goals and tickets have hands-on/review ranges, but the phase 2 goals G04–G07 are given only a single total range, with no hands-on/review split, so 'every goal' is not satisfied.

assertions.assertion: Ticket estimates match their goals, and the phase 1 total equals the sum of its goals and is compared with capacity after a reserve, high end included.
assertions.quote: sum 3.25–4.5 h. Six hours, taken as focused, minus a 25% reserve (1.5 h) leaves 4.5 h; the high end fits with no slack
assertions.reason: Ticket estimates match the plan table (1.0–1.5, 1.25–1.75, 1.0–1.25), the sum is correct (3.25–4.5), and it is compared to capacity after reserve including the high end.

assertions.assertion: Calendar waits (reviews, grants, provider verification) are listed separately from hours where they apply.
assertions.quote: No calendar waits.
assertions.reason: The plan explicitly states calendar waits are none, with each ticket carrying calendar_waits: none, and phase 2 lists the HR session date as a separate wait.

assertions.assertion: Phase 1 estimates fit about six hours of one person with a reserve, and the plan says which goals still give a demo if time runs out.
assertions.quote: Cut line if time runs short, in the order work stays useful: G01 (corpus is indexed and its gaps known) → G02 (demoable agent) → G03.
assertions.reason: The estimates fit within 6 hours after a 1.5h reserve, and the plan states which goals still yield a demo (G01+G02) if time runs out.

cases.note: The cases are the evaluation skill's own worked example, and its calibration reference describes what a good judgment does with them, so this is not a blind test.

assertions.assertion: Rejects a true width observation cited only to the question and accepts it when the answer span is selected.
assertions.quote: "case_id": "s03", ... "span_completeness": "incomplete", ... "support": "unsupported"
assertions.reason: s03 (question-only span) is rejected as unsupported and s04 (question plus answer) is accepted as supported, as required.

assertions.assertion: Separates valid identities from support, handles an omitted exception and rejects the unrelated half of a shared-excerpt pair.
assertions.quote: "case_id": "s09", ... "applicability": "not_applicable", ... "support": "unsupported"
assertions.reason: Valid identities are kept separate from support (s09, s15 valid but unsupported), the s07 omitted-exception contradiction is handled, and s09 is rejected against the shared excerpt that supports s08, so the assertion is met despite s05 being labelled differently.

assertions.assertion: Accepts written dimensions while rejecting unsupported physical inference from unscaled pixels.
assertions.quote: The task asks for the written width, and the quote states it. The unscaled-drawing caveat is irrelevant to a written value.
assertions.reason: s10 is accepted as supported on the written dimension and s11's pixel inference is rejected, even though the labels differ from the key (contradicted vs unsupported).

assertions.assertion: Distinguishes contradictions from absent evidence and records unresolved conflicting records.
assertions.quote: "contrary_evidence": "none", "support": "unsupported" ... Missing evidence is not a contradiction
assertions.reason: s13 (blank field) is unsupported rather than contradicted, s12 is contradicted, and s14 is unresolved with the conflicting records recorded.

assertions.assertion: Reports judgments and label disagreements as AI-only calibration evidence, without claiming independent human truth.
assertions.quote: The judgments are my own reading of the cases and the rubric.
assertions.reason: The answer does say the labels are AI-authored and provisional and should not be used as a quality gate without human review, but it does not describe the judgments or label disagreements as AI-only calibration evidence, and it reports no disagreement figures.

cases.note: The pack is the memory skill's own demonstration fixture and its generator script is installed with the skill, so the page contents are within the agent's reach; a separate pack would make this blind.

assertions.assertion: Classifies the header-only scanned page as low density and routes it to OCR or vision instead of passing it as a text page.
assertions.quote: "density_class": "image_only"
assertions.reason: The header-only scanned page is classed image_only (low density) and routed to ocr_or_vision, not passed as text.

assertions.assertion: Flags the table page and the drawing page and routes them to both text and image.
assertions.quote: "route": "text_and_image", "send": "native text plus rendered image"
assertions.reason: Both the table page and the drawing page are flagged (table and drawing hints) and routed to text and image.

assertions.assertion: Extracts the written dimension and the scale statement as separate fields and labels any pixel-derived value as an estimate.
assertions.quote: "written_dimensions": ["6.0 m"], "scale_statements": ["Scale 1:200 @ A3"]
assertions.reason: The dimension and scale are separate fields, and pixel-derived values are required to be labelled pixel_estimate; none were measured.

assertions.assertion: Sizes the image budget from the pack and labels the thresholds as defaults to calibrate.
assertions.quote: I set none. I suggest 150-200 dpi for the table and 200-300 dpi for the drawing
assertions.reason: The thresholds are labelled as uncalibrated defaults, but the image budget was not set; the report only gives a count of 3 images for a full visual pass and no budget, and it says none was set.

assertions.assertion: Reports that OCR and vision were not executed and keeps those pages unresolved rather than empty.
assertions.quote: "status": "UNRESOLVED: body content never read; no OCR or vision available in this trial"
assertions.reason: The report states OCR and vision were not run and keeps the scanned page unresolved rather than empty.

assertions.assertion: Scores document and operative-section coverage separately and fails the supplement-dependent question for a main-only retriever.
assertions.quote: "main_policy_only": ... False, (1, 2), (2, 3), {("maintenance-exception", "query_miss")}
assertions.reason: The control scores document coverage (1/2) and section coverage (2/3) separately and expects failure for the main-only retriever on the supplement-dependent question, though it was not run.

assertions.assertion: Distinguishes absent content, empty extraction, query miss, truncation and unviewed visuals.
assertions.quote: {("closure-notice", "empty_extraction"), ("closure-notice", "unviewed_visuals")}
assertions.reason: Controls expect distinct diagnoses for absent_content, empty_extraction, query_miss, section_truncation and unviewed_visuals.

assertions.assertion: Preserves an unresolved visual-evidence outcome and specifies the governed review path instead of interpreting empty text as no relevant provision.
assertions.quote: Reviewing the closure notice's image. The fixture has no image bytes, so the Route Cedar closure question stays unresolved.
assertions.reason: Unresolved status is preserved, but no governed review path is specified in the answer or code.

assertions.assertion: Retains manual golden queries as diagnostic evidence and does not claim they prove agent query formulation or real PDF extraction.
assertions.quote: I used `manual_golden` as the query origin, so nothing here counts as evidence of how the agent formulates queries.
assertions.reason: The answer retains manual golden queries as diagnostic and disclaims proof of agent query formulation, and it also states that real extraction was not run.
